title: Scholia lesson
description: content/courses/<course>/lessons/<id>.json. A lesson starts at a position and teaches lines from it as sections. Lessons and sections link to each other by position: a section continues the one whose end its line passes through, and a lesson continues the section that ends where it starts (or one move before). Lines may only part at a section's end, where the learner chooses.

course.description: The course's id; must match the directory.

summary.description: One line on what the lesson covers: a description, not a chess claim.

start.description: Moves from the initial position to where the lesson begins.

status.description: "reviewed" only once every explanation in the lesson is.

sections.description: The lines the lesson teaches. A section that shares moves with another branches from it; put sections in reading order.

title.description: Leads with the move that makes this line different, e.g. "7.Kg1: running to the corner"; learners choose sections by it.

kind.description: "main": a line to learn. "trap": the opponent's tempting mistake and how to punish it (or, facing an opening, the learner's pitfall).

line.description: The whole line from the lesson's start, including moves shared with the section it branches from (those are played as setup).

steps.description: Moves of the line to stop at, in order. Moves before the first step are played as setup.

move.description: The move's label: "8.g3" for White, "7...Qh4" for Black.

prompt.description: The learner's moves only: what they are asked to find.

accept.description: The learner's moves only: SAN of every move that counts as correct, including the line's own. The engine must rate each as sound.

disputed.description: The line follows a source the engine disagrees with; the player shows both views.
